subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should `memory_recall` expose model-visible UUIDs for `memory_forget(memoryId=...)`, or should stale/conflicting fact cleanup wait for the broader tombstone/supersede memory lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650?
rationale: The source and live repro prove the deletion-handoff gap, but the permanent contract affects model-visible identifiers, delete safety, privacy expectations, and future memory lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Approve Narrow UUID Handoff
options.body: Add model-visible UUIDs or an equivalent exact deletion selector to `memory_recall`, keep UUID validation unchanged, and leave automatic replacement/deprecation for the lifecycle tracker.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle MVP
options.body: Keep this issue open as concrete repro evidence but require the fix to land with review/edit/forget/tombstone/supersede storage semantics from the broader memory MVP.

options.title: Document Query-First Workaround
options.body: Document that users should call `memory_forget(query=...)` after recall, accepting the extra round trip and embedding-dependence for now.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow UUID Handoff
recommendation.body: Add model-visible UUIDs or an equivalent exact deletion selector to `memory_recall`, keep UUID validation unchanged, and leave automatic replacement/deprecation for the lifecycle tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema and event-journal history makes this the best available owner for the lifecycle-contract decision.
